item: Vacuous-fault reach audit, second pass over the uncovered stub shapes: one test whose secret-bearing transfer error was never reached is fixed with mutant proof, one stub-intent hardening
refs: parent sweep: R385 (follow-through of #1636); no PR number in the row
summary: The first audit left three shapes uncovered; measured now. Mock side_effect with an exception: one file (test_duckduckgo.py) 3 sites, both failure tests sound (mutant: the outer except re-raises -> red). Multi-line generator throw: 4 tests, all AssertionError must-not-call guards, zero reached is correct. Fake classes, dict-held or attribute stubs (any raise inside a non-test def referenced by a test other than as a direct call or call argument): 1036 tests reference one, 291 reached none of their non-guard raises, 36 picked by title for a failure claim and read by hand plus about 20 more, nearly all correct (a mode of a fake the test does not use, a stub reached through another test, a tripwire). Real: test_a_state_save_that_fails_after_a_download_failure_leaves_nothing_to_chain monkeypatched _save to raise on every call, so the first save INSIDE the download failed on the disk and the transfer error naming the passphrase was never reached; every HELD-not-in assertion was vacuous. Fixed (first save passes and the second fails and both are asserted) and proved by two source mutants green under the old test and red under the new: the stored error back to str(exc) and the failure logged with its text. Hardening without a distinguishing mutant: test_releasing_never_raises_on_a_broken_session never reached its in_transaction stub (the double lacked info, which the helper reads before it asks in_transaction); the double now has the attributes read before it and asserts it was asked. About 230 other unreached tests were scanned by title only. The weak-mention hole in the new guard was measured: zero instances in tests/.
